spiced.situation: John Sinclair is co-CRO (transitioning to full CRO) at IVigee Digital, a funded early-stage tech company with £1.5m/year in funding, a 15-man Silicon Valley dev team, and significant AI capability already in-house. He also runs a separate personal venture called Persuasion Jiu-Jitsu, where he operates as a fractional CRO/commercial engine builder for early-stage funded startups — helping them build GTM strategy, sales teams, and commercial infrastructure before they go to seed. He described his core work as: 'I build commercial engines... I go in as CRO effectively and build out your strategies and maps.' He is active on LinkedIn, familiar with AI tools including Claude, and is clearly well-networked at decision-maker level across multiple early-stage tech businesses.
spiced.pain: Two distinct pain contexts emerged. First, for IVigee Digital specifically: no pain was surfaced — they already have a large dev team and are fully resourced on AI. John explicitly closed that door. Second, and more relevantly for Notch, the pain John articulated was around the wider market he operates in — sales teams not reaching out, over-relying on technology, and unqualified pipeline being generated by junior BDRs who lack commercial judgement. He said: 'Half the problems I had with teams that I put in place, they're just not reaching out. Calling people, emailing, they're just expecting technology to do it for them.' He also described the broader RevOps/GTM AI deployment pain Sean opened with — integrations, guardrails, CRM hygiene, and adoption — as familiar and credible, even if not personally acute at IVigee right now.
spiced.impact: The operational impact John references is around wasted pipeline capacity and poor qualification in the teams he builds and advises. He told one of his sales reps this morning to 'stop filling your diary with useless crap' — indicating that low-quality, unqualified activity is a live issue in the companies he works with. Strategically, John is well-positioned as a connector and influencer: he is regularly approached for introductions and referrals at CRO/RevOps level, and explicitly said 'I get asked all the time' for exactly the kind of introductions Notch needs. The impact of winning John as a partner rather than a direct customer could be significant — he has ongoing access to multiple early-stage funded startups who are actively building commercial infrastructure and would be natural Notch prospects.
spiced.critical_event: No formal deadline or trigger event was mentioned for IVigee Digital — and John ruled them out as a near-term prospect entirely due to existing funding and dev resource. For his Persuasion Jiu-Jitsu work, he mentioned 'once the politics changes, I know there'll be different opportunities' which is vague and not a firm trigger. No budget cycle, contract renewal, or regulatory deadline was referenced. The meeting was booked for Wednesday at 11:15 (implied to be 4th June 2026) — the urgency here is relationship-driven rather than event-driven. The AE should not go in expecting a deal timeline; this is a partnership/referral conversation first.
spiced.decision: For IVigee Digital: John is co-CRO moving to CRO, but he explicitly stated they have a full Silicon Valley dev team, existing AI investment, and funding in place — he does not see himself as the right fit as a buyer there right now. For the Persuasion Jiu-Jitsu / partner angle: John is the sole decision-maker for his own consultancy. He indicated he can influence and introduce at decision-maker level within the startups he advises, saying 'I'm at that level so I get that I can influence the decision. So I'm a decision maker level.' No other stakeholders or sign-off processes were mentioned for the partner conversation. Budget was not discussed for any potential referral or partner arrangement.

objections.objection: IVigee Digital is not a viable prospect — they have £1.5m/year in funding, a 15-man Silicon Valley dev team already across AI, and John said plainly: 'that's a dead duck for you, that one.'
objections.response: Sean accepted this cleanly and pivoted quickly to exploring John's Persuasion Jiu-Jitsu work and the partner/referral angle. This was handled well — no attempt to push back or force the IVigee angle. The pivot preserved the conversation and kept John engaged.

objections.objection: John initially questioned whether Sean had done his homework — 'I'm just checking if you've done your homework, that's all' — probing whether Sean had actually researched IVigee Digital before calling.
objections.response: Sean's response was weak here. He stumbled and said 'Persuasive... Persuasion Jiu-Jitsu' which appeared to be him reading from a screen rather than demonstrating genuine research. John let it go, but the AE should be aware that John is sharp and will test preparation. Sean recovered through honesty and rapport rather than substance.

objections.objection: John noted that Notch specifically may not be relevant to him personally right now: 'not saying it wouldn't be a dead duck in the future because things are about to change.'
objections.response: This was partially addressed by framing the meeting as a partner/referral conversation rather than a direct sale. However, it was not probed further — the AE should explore what 'things about to change' means and whether there is a future direct opportunity within his consultancy work.

handovers.recommended_approach: Open by acknowledging this is a two-track conversation — you are not coming in to sell Notch to IVigee Digital. Frame it explicitly as: (1) understanding whether John could be a referral partner for Notch given his access to early-stage funded startups building commercial engines, and (2) giving John a proper look at what Notch does so he can make an informed decision about whether it is something worth pointing his network toward. This framing respects the dynamic John himself set up on the call. Do not pitch IVigee Digital — John will shut this down immediately and you will lose credibility. On the partner angle, probe specifically: how many early-stage companies is he actively working with right now, what does their typical AI and RevOps maturity look like, and at what stage does he usually bring in external tooling recommendations? John said he is 'always getting asked' for exactly the kind of introductions Notch needs — understand the volume and quality of that flow. Ask him to describe the profile of a company he would feel comfortable introducing Notch to. This helps qualify the partner opportunity without it feeling like an interrogation. On Notch's product, lead with the CRM automation and inbound lead routing use cases Sean mentioned — these resonated enough for John to stay on the call. John values qualification rigour highly (he explicitly coaches his teams on it), so frame Notch around the quality of commercial output, not just efficiency or volume. Tobiah should be prepared for John to ask sharp questions about how the product actually works in production — John is technically literate and commercially experienced, so avoid vague demos or high-level positioning. He will probe. Finally, explore the 'politics changing' comment — something is shifting in John's world that he thinks will open up opportunities. Understanding what that is could reveal a future direct buying opportunity or a near-term referral trigger.
key_quotes: Considering you're using my strategy every time. Always happy got 30 seconds. Go for it. — John acknowledged the cold call approach immediately, signalling he respects the method and practises it himself. This is a peer-level conversation, not a standard prospect meeting.

I'm at that level so I get that I can influence the decision. So I'm a decision maker level so you've got the right point on that front. But obviously sadly with IVigee I can't do any inquiry on that one. — John explicitly confirmed his influence and decision-making authority while cleanly closing the door on IVigee. The partner opportunity is the real one here.

I get asked all the time and because I'm now at a certain top level view perspective, I don't always have time to filter them out, but I'm always getting asked for exactly what you're after and what you're looking for. So if I can help you pass stuff on, then I'm more than happy to support you. — This is the core commercial opportunity. John has inbound demand for exactly what Notch offers and no current mechanism to refer it efficiently.

Half the problems I had with teams that I put in place, they're just not reaching out. Calling people, emailing, they're just expecting technology to do it for them. — John's articulation of a live pain in the companies he advises. This is the wedge for Notch — not AI for its own sake, but AI that supports human-led commercial activity rather than replacing it.
